title: BQP^cc is not contained in MA^cc
abstract: We exhibit a bipartite language with a poly-logarithmic quantum communication protocol and polynomial Merlin-Arthur communication complexity.
summary: This theoretical paper proves a separation between two quantum complexity classes, $	ext{BQP}^{	ext{cc}}$ and $	ext{MA}^{	ext{cc}}$, by analyzing a specific bipartite language. Using a lower-bound technique, the authors demonstrate that while the quantum communication cost is low (polylogarithmic), the Merlin-Arthur communication cost grows polynomially with the input size. This result significantly refines our understanding of the computational power achievable with quantum versus classical-assisted verification protocols.
main_problem: The paper aims to prove that the quantum communication complexity class $	ext{BQP}^{	ext{cc}}$ is not contained within the Merlin-Arthur communication complexity class $	ext{MA}^{	ext{cc}}$.
main_result:
By analyzing a specific bipartite language $G_n = 1 - 	ext{Cheat-Shapen}$, the authors show that its quantum communication complexity is polylogarithmic, while its Merlin-Arthur communication complexity grows at least as fast as $n^{1/4}$, thus establishing $	ext{BQP}^{	ext{cc}} 
ot\subseteq 	ext{MA}^{	ext{cc}}$.
method: The proof employs a lower-bound argument, building upon techniques from Klauck [2], by analyzing the acceptance probability of the protocol under specific distributions.
model_or_system: The analysis is performed on a bipartite language $L_n$ (specifically $G_n$) defined over inputs of size $N_n$, comparing the costs of quantum communication protocols ($	ext{Q}^{	ext{cc}}$) versus public-coin Merlin-Arthur protocols ($	ext{MA}^{	ext{cc}}$).
key_observables: The primary observable is the communication cost, comparing $	ext{Q}^{	ext{cc}}(G_n) \in O(\log^3 N_n)$ against $	ext{MA}^{	ext{cc}}(G_n) \in \Omega(n^{1/4})$.
important_parameters: The complexity measure depends on the input size $N_n$ and the error parameter $\epsilon$.
main_assumptions: The lower-bound argument relies on prior work by Klauck [2], and the final corollary assumes that the sequence $(N_n)_n$ is strictly monotone.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the complexity measures for quantum and Merlin-Arthur communication protocols, defines the specific bipartite language $G_n$, and then proceeds with a detailed lower-bound proof (Theorem 3.1) leading to the final separation result (Corollary 3.2).
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete separation result between two major complexity classes ($	ext{BQP}^{	ext{cc}}$ and $	ext{MA}^{	ext{cc}}$) using communication complexity, which is a fundamental topic in quantum information theory and computational complexity.
